preconditions.description: Input n must be a positive integer.

postconditions.expression: all(square in [i*i for i in range(1, int(n**0.5)+1)] for square in squares) and sum(squares) == n and len(squares) == return_value
postconditions.description: The output is the smallest number of perfect squares that sum to n, where squares is a list of perfect squares (1, 4, 9, ...) summing to n.
The output is at least 1, since n is positive and can always be expressed as the sum of at least one perfect square (itself if n is a perfect square).
